headline: Nvidia RTX 50 series prices jump up to 30% in South Korea
summary: TSMC wafer hikes and expensive GDDR7 memory modules are driving up costs for Nvidia's next-gen GPUs, with the RTX 5090 potentially exceeding $5,100.
details: Nvidia's upcoming RTX 50 series graphics cards are facing significant price increases in South Korea, with hikes reportedly reaching up to 30%. This surge is attributed to rising costs from TSMC for advanced process wafers and the increased price of GDDR7 memory modules, which are now costing $20 per unit.

These higher production costs are forcing Nvidia to increase the prices of its GPU packages sold to board partners. Consequently, these partners must pass the increased expenses onto consumers, leading to higher retail prices for the graphics cards.

Major manufacturers have reportedly suspended shipments ahead of an August price hike, with many companies scrambling to secure inventory before the increases take effect. Some manufacturers are considering price increases of around 20%, while others are preparing for hikes of up to 30%.

High-end graphics cards, particularly those with larger GDDR7 memory configurations, are expected to experience the most substantial price jumps. For example, the RTX 5060 Ti 8GB is now selling for approximately 700,000 won ($490), an increase of about 100,000 won ($70).

The RTX 5070 model has seen a roughly 200,000 won ($140) increase, now listed at around 1.1 million won ($770). The flagship RTX 5090 is facing the most dramatic price hike, with some models reaching up to 7.3 million won ($5,112), an increase of as much as 1.5 million won ($1,050) from last month.
